ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OP$ bisects $\angle MON$, and point $C$ is any point on $OP$ with $CA\perp ON$ at foot $A$. The perpendicular bisector of line segment $OA$, denoted as $BG$, intersects $OM$ at point $B$ and intersects $OA$ at point $G$. Given $AB=6$ and $AC=3$, what is the area of $\triangle OBC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw line $CE\perp OM$ at point E. Since $OP$ bisects $\angle MON$, $CA\perp ON$, and $CE\perp OM$, it follows that $CE=CA=3$. Since $BG$ is the perpendicular bisector of $OA$, we have $BA=BO=6$. The area of $\triangle OBC$ is given by $S_{\triangle OBC}=\frac{1}{2}\times OB\times CE=\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 3=\boxed{9}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, O is at the lower left, ON is a lower horizontal ray to the right, OM is an oblique ray from O toward the upper right, and OP is a ray between OM and ON and passes through point C. From point C, a perpendicular is drawn downward to ON, with foot A; there is a right-angle mark at A in the figure. The line BG passing through G and B is perpendicular to OA; there is a right-angle mark at G in the figure, and B lies on ray OM. The figure also connects line segments such as BA and BC. Then reason: According to the problem, OP bisects ∠MON, and C is on the angle bisector. Suppose a perpendicular is drawn from C to OM, with foot E. The perpendicular distances from a point on the angle bisector to the two sides of the angle are equal, so CE = CA = 3. Also because BG is the perpendicular bisector of OA, and B is on BG, the distances from B to O and A are equal, that is, BO = BA. It is known that AB = 6, therefore OB = 6. Taking OB as the base of △OBC, since OB lies on OM, the perpendicular distance from C to OM is CE = 3, so S_△OBC = 1/2 × OB × CE = 1/2 × 6 × 3 = 9.
